newsitem.title: USA: Low export shipments hit CBOT nearby soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Low export shipments hit CBOT nearby soybeans.

text.p: Low weekly soybean export shipments indicated by the U.S. Department of Agriculture pushed CBOT soybean futures lower at midsession Monday, floor traders and analysts said.
"I guess there's a little disappointment over the export sales," said one Chicago-based analyst.
USDA put weekly export inspection shipments at 8.9 million bushels. That figure fell below trade expectations for 10 million to 15 million bushels.
Weakness from the export data was limited to nearby contracts, traders said.
Heavy commodity fund-inspired losses in CBOT soymeal futures also weighed on soymeal prices, traders said.
Refco, R.J. O'Brien, Rosenthal Collins and Smith Barney were all noted sellers in the soymeal pit near midsession Monday, floor traders said.

Traders have been watching for signs that the bulk of demand for soybeans from world markets was shifting to South America so many interpreted the low export shipments figure as a sign that demand for U.S. soybeans was falling.
At 1112 CBOT soybeans were up nine cents a bushel to down 7-1/2 cents, with July down 7-3/4 at $8.38.
